newsitem.title: CANADA: Canadian bonds open stronger after U.S. PPI data.
newsitem.headline: Canadian bonds open stronger after U.S. PPI data.

text.p: Canadian bonds opened stronger on Wednesday, although spreads to U.S. issues widened as a tame U.S. producer price index report increased expectations that U.S. rates would not rise next week, dealers said.
"Canada is going up on the heels of the U.S. PPI number, which came in much better than expected," said Will Sutherland, vice president of fixed-income with Altamira Investment Services Inc.
Canada's 30-year benchmark bond rose C$0.13 to C$110.73 to yield 7.091 percent.
The U.S. 30-year bond rose 16/32 to yield 6.88 percent. The spread between the bonds widened to 21 basis points from 18 basis points at the close of trading on Tuesday.

Canadian and U.S. fixed-income markets strengthened on Wednesday after the Labor Department reported that the producer price index fell 0.6 percent in April, compared with expectations that it would remain unchanged.

The report was seen reducing the likelihood that the U.S. Federal Reserve would hike rates at next week's meeting of its Open Market Committee. A U.S. rate hike would likely weaken the Canadian bond market.
"We're still locked in the trading range here," said Sutherland. "Everyone's waiting until the FOMC meeting next week."

Analysts said the market was now looking ahead to the release on Thursday of U.S. consumer price index data for April for further clues about whether the Fed will move. Canada will also release consumer price index data on Thursday for April.
In other prices, Canada's 10-year benchmark bond rose C$0.25 to C$103.25 to yield 6.536 percent. The U.S. 10-year bond rose 12/32 to yield 6.66 percent.
The negative spread between the two bonds narrowed to 12 basis points from 15 basis points at the close of trading on Tuesday.
The three-month cash T-bill traded with a yield of 3.07 percent against its U.S. equivalent which yielded 5.19 percent.
